claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
A portion of Hf and Ta in HfMoTaTiZr should be substituted with Ti and Zr.
Hf and Ta are relatively heavy elements, whereas Ti and Zr are lighter substitution elements.
Replacing heavier refractory elements with lighter elements can reduce RHEA density.
The proposed substitution can reduce HfMoTaTiZr density without sacrificing its room- and high-temperature mechanical performance.
The modified alloy will remain a high-entropy alloy after the substitution.
The modified alloy will have a BCC crystal structure.
The high-entropy effect will maintain solid-solution strengthening after substitution.
Maintained solid-solution strengthening will preserve the modified alloy's mechanical properties.
The modified alloy will have a lower density than as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy will maintain yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
The modified alloy will have room-temperature fracture toughness comparable to or better than as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.
The hypothesis is intended to apply from room temperature through 1000 °C under both compression and tension.
Alloys with varying amounts of heavy-to-light element substitution will be compared by density, room-temperature and 1000 °C yield strength, and room-temperature fracture toughness.
A modified alloy with yield strength below 700 MPa at 1000 °C is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.
A significant decrease in room-temperature fracture toughness relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000 °C, but the rejection threshold is below 700 MPa. Results from 700 to 800 MPa would violate the predicted outcome without falsifying the hypothesis.

The hypothesis is existential—that a suitable substitution can achieve the target—but the rule says failure of any modified alloy falsifies it. One unsuccessful substitution level does not falsify the possibility that another level could succeed.
